correctness.rationale: The cyclic-to-linear factor-two bound applies on this nonconstant primitive interval. Independently, among sorted rotations starting with a letter a, first come those whose first non-a letter is below a, then those for which it is above a. In the former group the last rotation has maximal initial a-streak in that group, and in the latter the first rotation has maximal streak. These terminal/initial rotations cannot have predecessor a, as prepending that a would give a longer streak in the same group. Since consecutive L entries differ, pair each L=F rotation in the below group with its successor and in the above group with its predecessor. This injects matches into mismatches, which count input cyclic boundaries. For the upper bound, independently reconstructed 80 inverse words by stable inverse-permutation traversal, sorted their rotations from scratch and checked primitivity, all last columns, linear runs n, and cyclic runs (n+1)//2. A ternary witness keeps all lexicographic comparisons in every larger stated ordered alphabet. Constant-necklace conventions and sentinel variants are outside the claim. Replay: /workspace/branches/independent_replays/replay3.py with the frozen BWT_WITNESSES.tsv, output replay3.out (ALL_80_ROTATION_CENSUSES_OK). This is a finite certificate, not extrapolation.

evidence: Kumallagov proves U_k(n)>=ceil(n/2) generally and attains it at p-1,p under p=5 mod 8 and primitive root 2; the qualifying primes for this interval are 101 and 149. General attainment from n>=7 is Conjecture 7.1, not a proved dominating theorem. Fici et al. prove unclustered existence without the input objective.
